You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".


The data files for this task are in your current working directory:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv
Read them from disk. Give your answer as your final message — do not write it to a file.
turns.answer_text:
My analysis approach: I built an ensemble (CatBoost on the raw stack strings + gradient boosting/random forest on per-component material tokens) trained on the 300 measured recipes, validated ~0.40+ Spearman rank CV, and averaged predictions over 10 seeds. Then I sanity-checked the top picks against device physics. Rankings were stable across seeds.

**Device-physics reasoning for the picks**

The training data shows what works: clean glass-ITO/FTO substrates; fullerene ETLs (PCBM-60, C60) capped with a thin hole-blocker/encapsulator such as BCP (or Bphen/PEI-style modifiers) that pin the quasi-Fermi level, suppress interface recombination, and stop back-metal diffusion; p-type polymeric HTLs like PTAA or P3CT-Na (well matched energy levels to MAPbI3's valence band, hydrophobic → smooth absorber growth); and Cu or Ag back contacts. Top training recipes (18–25% median PCE) all follow exactly this pattern.

- **c044** — SLG|ITO, PCBM-60|BCP ETL, PTAA HTL, Cu, spin-coating. The canonical high-selectivity inverted stack: PCBM extraction, BCP hole-blocking cap, PTAA's ideal band alignment, Cu back electrode. All-time training favorites. Highest predicted PCE (~17.8).
- **c088** — Willow glass|ITO (ultrathin flexible glass, still a proper TCO), C60|BCP ETL, PTAA, Cu, doctor blading. Blade-coating of the absorber is at least as good as spin-coating in train (a matched train recipe with C60|BCP/none-HTL/Cu via blade hit 18.4%) — adding PTAA improves on it.
- **c085** — SLG|ITO, TTC|C60|BCP, PTAA, Ag. Same PTAA/C60/BCP design logic with a thin TTC adhesion/interfacial underlayer; Ag contact fine.
- **c097 / c058** (statistically tied) — SLG|ITO, C60|BCP with a co-deposited n-type assistant (ITCPTC-Se: selenium-substituted acceptor with stronger intermolecular coupling, or a C60;PDI blend) and P3CT-Na (optimal p-type polymeric HTL in train). Extra interlayers shouldn't change the rank much; both land in the top tier.
- Next-best rejected: c030 (PTAA|PMMA + Al, close), c010 (raw C60 without blocker), c029/c076 (PEDOT:PSS + PET|ITO plastic — PEDOT is meh, PET|ITO loses a bit vs glass), c041 (NiMgLiO-c on FTO — plausible but single-sample HTL claim).

Final: c044, c088, c085, c097, c058
